title: Mexican-Style Pinto Beans (Instant Pot)

ingredients.name: Dried Pinto Beans
ingredients.notes: rinsed and sorted, no soaking needed

ingredients.name: Chicken Broth
ingredients.notes: or vegetable broth to keep vegetarian

ingredients.name: Jalapeño or Chipotle
ingredients.notes: halved, seeds removed for less heat

ingredients.name: Dried Epazote
ingredients.notes: optional but traditional; substitute dried oregano

steps: Rinse and sort the dried pinto beans, discarding any shriveled beans or debris. No soaking is required.
Set the Instant Pot to Sauté (Normal). Add lard or olive oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the halved onion cut-side down and the smashed garlic cloves. Sauté for 3–4 minutes until lightly golden and fragrant.
Add the cumin, chili powder, smoked paprika, and Mexican oregano. Stir and cook for 1 minute to bloom the spices.
Pour in the chicken broth and water, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Add the rinsed pinto beans, jalapeño, bay leaves, and epazote (if using). Stir to combine. Do NOT add salt yet — it can toughen the bean skins.
Secure the lid, set the vent to Sealing, and cook on Manual / Pressure Cook (High) for 45 minutes.
Allow the pressure to release naturally for 20 minutes, then carefully quick-release any remaining pressure.
Remove and discard the onion halves, jalapeño, and bay leaves.
Stir in the salt, taste, and adjust seasoning. For creamier beans, use a wooden spoon or potato masher to smash about one-quarter of the beans against the side of the pot.
Serve topped with fresh cilantro and a squeeze of lime juice.
notes: Salt is added after cooking — adding it beforehand can prevent beans from fully softening. If your beans are very old (over a year), increase cook time to 50–55 minutes. Leftovers keep in the fridge for up to 5 days and freeze well for 3 months. Use these as a base for refried beans by mashing and frying in a skillet with a little lard or oil.
